app.title: LensAudit · mass–light morphology audit of lensing maps
app.summary: A person picks a curated survey target or uploads their own pair of co-registered FITS products, either a science image plus a convergence map or a stack of model realizations. A validation tab instead runs a seeded synthetic cluster with known truth. The tool normalizes both maps, fits one scale between them and computes a residual and an ensemble-aware discrepancy score, with smoothing and the score threshold set in a sidebar. The person reads a headline metric strip, a four-panel figure with mass contours over light, the residual and score maps, machine warnings and a list of ways the map could be falsified. They export a JSON evidence receipt and the discrepancy map as FITS.

task.text: Check where an independently reconstructed mass map and a telescope image's light disagree, and how far that disagreement survives differences between models, then export a receipt of the audit.

data.text: A pair of co-registered 2D FITS rasters on one sky grid: an intensity image and a convergence map, or a cube of several model realizations of that map.
data.item: one pixel of a co-registered image and mass-map pair, or one model realization in the ensemble

stage.text: auditing published lens-model products against imaging, after the reconstruction and before any claim is reported

mechanism.text: Sliders in a sidebar set smoothing and the score threshold. Three tabs load the input pair from prepared archive products, uploaded files or a seeded synthetic test. The audit then reruns and fills a metric strip, a four-panel figure, warnings and export buttons below the tabs.

field.text: mass–light comparison of gravitational-lensing convergence maps against imaging in astrophysics

workflow.name: compare two co-registered maps and score where they disagree

steps.here: Choose a curated survey target and open its prepared local products, upload an image FITS and a κ FITS or ensemble, or run a seeded synthetic injected-offset test

steps.step: set the parameters of the computation
steps.here: Sidebar sliders set the light-proxy Gaussian smoothing in pixels and the discrepancy-score threshold

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Background-subtract and smooth the light, robust-normalize both maps, fit one scale α, then compute the residual R = K − αL, a score scaled by ensemble scatter with a floor, and the mass and light centroids

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Metric strip with centroid offset, model spread, area above threshold and number of lens realizations; a 2×2 figure with the light proxy, mass contours over light with both centroids, the residual map and the score map

steps.step: check the result against stated limits
steps.here: Machine warnings (single model, few realizations, large discrepancy area) and a fixed checklist of what could falsify the map
Download a JSON evidence receipt with inputs, parameters, results and warnings, and the discrepancy-score map as FITS

distinctive: The input must be a pair, a light image and an independently reconstructed mass map. Image-only inference is refused, and mismatched grids or missing WCS stop the audit.
An ensemble of model realizations gives the scatter that scales the discrepancy score, with a systematic floor so a single model cannot claim certainty.
Synthetic known-truth data is kept in a separate validation tab, apart from the real observational targets.
Archive products are fetched, hashed and reprojected outside the UI by CLI commands, and the console only opens the verified, prepared files.
